text:
Arona — Landed late, the sea in the dark
The flight in at four, the hire car, the wrong turning twice. The apartment smelt of salt and someone else's sun cream. You heard the sea before you saw it.
Tomorrow: find the bakery and the beach, nothing more.
A day of what happened.

Arona — Black sand and a bakery
The bakery by the roundabout, the black sand too hot by eleven. Both kids in the water until their lips went blue. You read four pages and fell asleep under the umbrella.
A day of what happened.

Arona — The couple who looked so sure
The couple at the next table, matching and quiet, and the story you told yourself about them: that they had it all worked out. Then the thought that someone might tell the same story about you.
Tomorrow: the drive north.
A day of what you made of it.

Puerto de la Cruz — Tight in the chest on the mountain road
The bends and the drop, your hands tight on the wheel and something tight in your chest that stayed after you parked. Then the warm old square, and your shoulders letting go.
A day of what you felt.

Puerto de la Cruz — The pools by the sea wall
The pools by the sea wall, the waves coming over, your eldest counting the big ones. Wrinkled potatoes and green sauce at a plastic table. Rain for ten minutes and nobody minded.
Tomorrow: Garachico, and the rock pools there.
A day of what happened.

Garachico — A town built on what buried it
The town the lava buried, built again on top. You kept turning it over: the rock pools you swam in were made by the thing that ruined it. It felt as if it said something about you, and you are not sure it does.
A day of what you made of it.

Garachico — Closing the laptop
The laptop on the table all evening. You answered the two that mattered and chose to close it for the rest of the week. You told your partner, so it would hold.
Tomorrow: back south, the long way round by the coast.
A day of a choice.

Arona — Monday, arriving early
Monday arrived in your head on the drive back: the inbox, the meeting you have been putting off. You pictured it going badly, then going fine. Neither has happened yet.
Tomorrow: a slow morning, nothing before ten.
A day of what’s ahead.

Arona — Lizards and the first quiet
A slow morning by the pool. The kids in fits over lizards on the wall, your youngest laughing. The first morning without email. Monday is there, not dreaded, just known.
Tomorrow: walk up to the old town before it gets hot.
A day of what happened.
